Businesswoman Lily Tang Williams pulled out a win in New Hampshire's 2nd Congressional District primary against three other Republican candidates.

Four GOP candidates sought to earn the opportunity to flip red the district that spans the entire western part of the state north to south.

Tang Williams, who was also the 2024 nominee for the seat, emerged victorious over the rest of the field. An entrepreneur and co-chair of the New Hampshire Asian American Coalition from the town of Weare, Tang Williams dominated the race from a fundraising perspective. She hauled in nearly $1.2 million, while second place finisher Victor Orlando raised $175,000.

Tang Williams is a Chinese immigrant who describes herself as a survivor of communism — she pitched herself as an "open-minded" and "independent" person in an April interview with WMUR, signaling her willingness to oppose President Donald Trump when appropriate for her would-be constituents.

The New Hampshire State House, the state capitol building of New Hampshire, is seen on February 16, 2023 in Concord, New Hampshire. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)

Asked specifically about the conflict in Iran, she denounced oppressive regimes and said she would like Trump to provide a plan for ending the war and reaching a peace agreement. She also denounced politicians she said used their offices to enrich themselves.

TRUMP-BACKED NOMINEES DOMINATE PRIMARY CONTESTS AS PRESIDENT TIGHTENS PARTY VICE GRIP

Tang Williams formerly chaired the state's Libertarian Party.

Two other candidates in the race, Dan Nicholson and Michael Anthony Callis, captured only tiny percentages of the vote.

The Pinkham Notch Visitor Center is shown on a clear autumn day in New Hampshire’s White Mountain National Forest, Oct. 8, 2022. The center sits below Mount Washington, where search crews recovered the body of a missing Florida man on July 18, 2025. (Marli Miller/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

$50 TRILLION IN DEBT IS NOT A DISTANT THREAT. AMERICA IS SPEEDING TOWARDS IT

Both Tang Williams and Orlando pitched themselves as only center-right, in a state heavily controlled by Democrats.

New Hampshire, which has only one other congressional district, is a reliably blue state, though in her 2024 run, Tang Williams earned 47% of the vote.

The district is currently represented by Rep. Maggie Goodlander (D-N.H.).

articles.title: Marco Rubio says US seeks more economic and security ties in Latin America
articles.excerpt: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says President Donald Trump’s administration hopes to ink trade deals with Colombia, Peru and Ecuador soon, as Washington seeks greater ties with right-wing allies ac...
articles.body_text:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says President Donald Trump’s administration hopes to ink trade deals with Colombia, Peru and Ecuador soon, as Washington seeks greater ties with right-wing allies across Latin America.

Rubio met with Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella during a visit to Barranquilla on Tuesday, part of a three-nation trip aimed at consolidating relationships with allied governments and expanding US military involvement in the region.

“We have a lot of common interest with them, both taking on regional transnational criminal terrorism and also economic engagements,” Rubio said of the three countries before departing. “It’s part of a trend that you’re seeing in the Western Hemisphere of alignment with US and US interests.”

In addition to Colombia, the US secretary of state is set to travel later this week to Ecuador and Peru to meet with their respective presidents, Daniel Noboa and Keiko Fujimori.

Before his departure to Colombia, Rubio explained that Washington was seeking “good, solid” trade deals in the near future with all three countries.

The diplomatic tour also comes as the Trump administration seeks to check China’s growing influence in Latin America.

China, for example, signed a free-trade agreement with Peru in 2009 and has since become the South American country’s top trading partner, beating the US.

The Trump administration has also pushed for greater control over the entire Western Hemisphere as part of a policy platform informally called the “Donroe Doctrine”.

Security has been the centrepiece of that effort. Since taking office for a second term, Trump has authorised lethal military actions in Venezuela, the eastern Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea, which he touted as critical to combat drug trafficking.

De la Espriella took office in August, promising a return to a militarised approach towards crime and armed groups, in line with Trump’s priorities.

He has also pledged to pursue closer relations with the US, after clashes between Trump and former President Gustavo Petro, Colombia’s first elected leftist leader.

“Colombia wants to re-establish itself as the United States’ primary partner in hemispheric security,” De la Espriella said after his meeting with Rubio, which included the signing of agreements on critical minerals and civil nuclear cooperation.

De la Espriella indicated he would seek US support for military operations, including through radar and drone technology.

A political newcomer with no prior experience in elected office, de la Espriella has been part of a wave of right-wing victories across Latin America in recent years.

The Trump administration has buttressed the electoral campaigns of the region’s conservative candidates by pledging financial and political support.

He has also invited them to join the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition (ACCC), or the “Shield of the Americas”, a regional security framework that emphasises US military involvement to combat drugs and crime.

Leftist presidential candidate Ivan Cepeda, a Petro ally, slammed Rubio’s visit to Colombia as an “act of surrendering strategic aspects of our sovereignty”, pointing to Tuesday’s mineral and energy deals.

Cepeda also criticised de la Espriella’s decision to loosen gun restrictions on the same day, a position that echoes Trump administration policy.

“Just how disastrous the ‘memoranda of understanding’ that Rubio and De la Espriella are set to sign must be, given that an equally disastrous decision — the authorisation to carry weapons — is being announced at the same time,” Cepeda wrote on social media.

De la Espriella has defended his decision, however, citing Colombia’s struggles with crime and its six-decade-long internal conflict.

“For years, law-abiding citizens faced restrictions while criminals continued to arm themselves illegally to the teeth. That has to change,” he said in a social media post.

Colombia has asked the Trump administration to lower tariffs imposed on the country in July.

First-term Republican Governor Kelly Ayotte easily handled her p...
articles.body_text:
Leftist candidate Karishma Manzur is trying to upset 4-term Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas in New Hampshire’s Democratic Senate primary.

First-term Republican Governor Kelly Ayotte easily handled her primary opponents Tuesday, setting up a high-stakes general election battle against Democratic gubernatorial nominee Cinde Warmington, who ran unopposed for her party's nomination.

Ayotte defeated Republican challengers Shaun Fife and Bob Wayne McClory as she seeks a second two-year term leading the Granite State.

The former senator and state Attorney General entered Tuesday's primary as the incumbent after winning the governor's mansion in 2024, when Ayotte defeated former Manchester Mayor Joyce Craig and kept the office in Republican hands following the retirement of four-term GOP Gov. Chris Sununu.

KEY SWING STATE VOTERS TO SETTLE DUELING SENATE PRIMARY FIGHTS IN CRUCIAL OPEN-SEAT RACE

New Hampshire Gov. Kelly Ayotte marches in the annual Independence Day parade in Amherst, N.H., on July 4, 2026. (Gov. Kelly Ayotte)

Ayotte previously served as New Hampshire's attorney general from 2004 to 2009 before winning election to the U.S. Senate in 2010. She served one term before narrowly losing her 2016 reelection campaign to Democrat Maggie Hassan.

In 2024, following Sununu's decision not to seek a fifth two-year term, Ayotte mounted a political comeback with the outgoing governor's endorsement.

Former Republican Sen. John E. Sununu of New Hampshire is interviewed by Fox News Digital, on Sept.15, 2025 in Rye, N.H. (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News Digital)

In her first term, Ayotte successfully pushed to roll back portions of the state's bail reform law, arguing the existing system was too lenient on criminal suspects awaiting trial, signed legislation requiring public schools to restrict student cellphone use and pushed penalties for motorists who refuse Breathalyzer tests.

TRUMP-BACKED JOHN E. SUNUNU BREAKS WITH PRESIDENT ON KEY ISSUE AHEAD OF HIGH-STAKES NEW-HAMPSHIRE PRIMARY

Meanwhile, her tenure has faced criticism from the left over a state budget that included cuts to state agencies.

Ayotte will take on Warmington, who served on New Hampshire's five-member Executive Council for two terms, during which she was the lone Democrat on the body that works with the governor to approve state measures and helps consider gubernatorial appointments, among its duties. Tuesday marked her second campaign for governor after Warmington lost the 2024 Democratic gubernatorial primary.

Warmington has attacked Ayotte for failing to adequately stand up to President Donald Trump, citing healthcare cuts, tariffs and the war in Iran.

Former Executive Councilor Cinde Warmington of New Hampshire, seen in a campaign video launches her second straight bid for governor of the key northern New England swing state. (Cinde Warmington for governor)

The Concord Monitor reported in June that Ayotte "steered clear of all things Trump" for much of her first term, noting that, when asked whether she would stand with Trump if he visited New Hampshire, Ayotte responded, "I'm standing with the people of New Hampshire."

Alec Schemmel is a Politics Reporter for Fox News Digital who is originally from Charlotte, North Carolina but now resides in the Washington D.C.-Baltimore Metro Area.

articles.title: US attacks 5 Iranian oil tankers, Tehran retaliates with strikes on Jordan
articles.excerpt:
US bombs five Iranian oil tankers after its navy is attacked

The United States has launched attacks on five Iranian oil tankers in the Gulf of Oman and near Kharg Island after accusing Tehran of laun...
articles.body_text:
US bombs five Iranian oil tankers after its navy is attacked

The United States has launched attacks on five Iranian oil tankers in the Gulf of Oman and near Kharg Island after accusing Tehran of launching ballistic missiles at a US warship twice in two days.

Iran responded to Tuesday’s attacks by firing missiles at US forces stationed at the Al Azraq base in Jordan.

Amman said its air defences intercepted and destroyed 18 of 20 Iranian missiles, while the rest fell in open areas.

The exchange of fire comes amid escalating tensions in the Gulf six months into the US and Israel’s war on Iran, with Tehran maintaining the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and Washington enforcing a naval blockade on Iranian ports.

The hostilities briefly drove oil prices to $99.46 earlier on Tuesday.

In a statement, US Central Command (CENTCOM) said Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) had sought to target a US warship twice over the past two days, but the vessel “successfully evaded the attempted Iranian attacks”.

“No American personnel were harmed,” it said.

CENTCOM said it retaliated by striking and destroying the Iranian oil carriers, M/T Kaviz, M/T Charminar, M/T Horizon 1, and M/T Riesco in the Gulf of Oman, as well as M/T Derya near Kharg Island.

“American forces directed the crews to abandon ship before the vessels were struck and rendered inoperable,” CENTCOM added.

Iran’s IRIB state broadcaster confirmed the attack near Kharg Island, which handled some 90 percent of the country’s oil exports before the war. It reported that the crew was evacuated and said a second tanker was hit near the southern port of Jask in the Gulf of Oman.

The IRGC also said that “several” Iranian commercial ships were hit, and that it retaliated by subjecting Al Azraq base in Jordan to “fierce missile strikes”. It claimed that hangars used by US fighter jets were destroyed in the attacks.

The IRGC went on to say that the earlier ballistic missile attacks on the US Navy DDG-119 and DDG-53 destroyers caused “significant damage… to these vessels”.

The Revolutionary Guard also threatened to target oil tankers in Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports, warning crews there to evacuate immediately.

“We warn all the crews of oil tankers in the Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports… to immediately abandon their vessels, whether at anchor or at the ports, because they will be targeted,” it said.

Jordan’s Armed Forces, meanwhile, said its air defences engaged 20 ballistic missiles, “successfully intercepting and destroying 18 of them”. Two missiles “fell in unpopulated areas”, it said in a statement.

The attacks did not cause any casualties, and specialised teams “have begun securing the locations where debris and shrapnel fell”, the military added.

Earlier, the chief of staff of Iran’s Armed Forces, Ali Abdollahi, had warned that Tehran would strike US military installations across the region if Iranian tankers were targeted.

“The US aggressor army has given Iranian oil tankers an evacuation warning to hit them, so I announce that any attack on Iranian oil tankers will result in the targeting of US bases in the region by the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran,” Abdollahi said on state television.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, however, said Washington would continue to strike Iranian ships.

“Iran continues to try to hit US naval ships, and for every time they do that or try to do that, they’re going to lose tankers,” Rubio told reporters on a visit to Colombia.

articles.title: Trump-backed John Sununu wins New Hampshire Republican Senate primary

Frontrunner Sununu beats Scott Brown to earn Republican nod in closely watched race in November

Former senator John E Sununu triumphed on Tuesday in the New Hampshire Republican Senate primary Scott ...
articles.body_text:
Frontrunner Sununu beats Scott Brown to earn Republican nod in closely watched race in November

Former senator John E Sununu triumphed on Tuesday in the New Hampshire Republican Senate primary Scott Brown, earning the GOP nod in what will likely be a must-win race if Democrats hope to seize the upper chamber.

Sununu, 61, was the clear frontrunner in the GOP primary. He served one term in the Senate from 2003 to 2009.

Brown represented Massachusetts, later moved to New Hampshire, and served as US ambassador to New Zealand and Samoa during Donald Trump’s first term.

The US president threw his support behind Sununu earlier this year, despite the former lawmaker’s past criticism of Trump, including a 2024 op‑ed in which Sununu called Trump a “loser” and backed Nikki Haley in the Republican presidential primary.

On the trail, Sununu has tried to show daylight between himself and the administration, criticizing Trump’s tariff policy, urging Congress to rein in executive power, and questioning the decision to launch military action in Iran.

He told New Hampshire Public Radio it was “a tactical mistake” to go to war “without having a plan for protecting the strait of Hormuz”. That posture may matter in a state where Trump’s approval rating sits at 38%.

Sununu and Brown did not respond to the Guardian’s interview requests.

Kristen Cianci, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee (RNC), said Sununu was a “strong candidate” who was “well positioned to beat out Pappas” in a general election. “While Democrats have been consumed by infighting, Republicans have been laser-focused on real issues like affordability and security,” she added in a statement.

Sununu will face congressman Chris Pappas, who beat back a progressive challenger in the Democratic primary, advancing as most observers expected to what will be a closely watched general election that is critical to Democratic hopes of flipping the upper chamber.

Some Democrats, however, worry New Hampshire could become a sleeper risk – a state where Republicans control the legislature but haven’t won a Senate race since 2010, when Kelly Ayotte, now the governor, captured a seat.

articles.excerpt:
Former GOP Sen. John E. Sununu pushes back on Trump Canadian tariffs, dismisses need for outside campaign help, in Fox News Digital interview.

Former Sen. John E. Sununu on Tuesday won the GOP Senate...
articles.body_text:
Former GOP Sen. John E. Sununu pushes back on Trump Canadian tariffs, dismisses need for outside campaign help, in Fox News Digital interview.

Former Sen. John E. Sununu on Tuesday won the GOP Senate nomination in swing state New Hampshire, in a race that may determine if Republicans keep control of the chamber in the midterm elections.

Sununu defeated former Sen. Scott Brown, the Associated Press reports, in the showdown to succeed retiring longtime Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, the first woman in the nation's history elected governor and senator.

Republicans haven't won a Senate election in New Hampshire in 16 years, but they view the open Democrat-held seat as a top flip opportunity in the fight to hold their slim majority in the midterms.

Sununu will now face off in the general election against either four-term Rep. Chris Pappas or socialist candidate and scientist Karishma Manzur, who are battling for the Democratic nomination.

THESE 12 MIDTERM RACES WILL DECIDE WHICH PARTY CONTROLS THE SENATE

Former Republican Sen. John E. Sununu of New Hampshire is running in the 2026 midterm elections to return to the Senate. (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News Digital)

Sununu, the son of former Gov. John H. Sununu and older brother to former Gov. Chris Sununu, is a former congressman and senator who is aiming to return to the Senate.

President Donald Trump in February endorsed Sununu, a longtime GOP Trump critic, over Brown, one of Trump's first-term ambassadors. Sununu was also backed by Senate Majority Leader John Thune and the National Republican Senatorial Committee.

Brown charged in a Fox News Digital interview that Sununu's "got 70 endorsements on his website, but he doesn't have the president’s. He never talks about it. He's embarrassed by it."

"I've had the MAGA base and a lot of those so-called traditional Republicans for almost over a year," Brown highlighted. "Johnny came lately, and he's here, and now he thinks everyone's going to just vote for him. That's not how it works. You got to go earn it."

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

Brown claimed that Sununu is "beholden" to Trump, Thune, the Senate leadership, and outside groups.

"He owes them everything. He doesn't work for the people of New Hampshire," Brown charged.

But Sununu told Fox News Digital, "I'll have one job stand up for the people of New Hampshire every single day... I don't need to make anyone in Washington happy. It's all about our state, our communities, our economy, and our small businesses."

Asked by about Trump's endorsement, Sununu didn't mention the president's name but highlighted his local endorsements, saying "we've received tremendous support in New Hampshire... we've got great momentum at the grassroots level."

Trump last week said he'd be heading out on the campaign trail to help fellow Republicans running in the midterms.

Asked if he'd like Trump to join him on the Granite State campaign trail, Sununu answered, "I don't need anyone from outside New Hampshire to campaign for me. I've said that from the very beginning."

Sen. Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), the first woman elected governor and U.S. senator in the nation's history, is retiring after her current term concludes later this year. (Getty Images)

The former senator also disagreed with the Trump administration's trade war with neighboring Canada, saying "I don't think it's the right thing to pick a trade war with Canada. They're a great trading partner for New Hampshire."

Republicans are facing a rough political climate heading into the midterms, due persistent inflation, high gas prices fueled by what polls indicate is an unpopular war with Iran, and Trump's underwater approval ratings.

But Sununu, who defeated Shaheen in 2002 to win election to the Senate but lost a rematch to her six years later, said he's "focused on the right things, affordability, bringing down the cost of living on housing, health care, and energy, a reform agenda."

Paul Steinhauser covers the national campaign trail from coast to coast for Fox News

articles.body_text:
Centcom says ‘defective’ drone was surveilling regional waters and was not collecting sensitive data

Iranian forces claimed to have seized an American underwater drone in the strait of Hormuz that the US military said had “malfunctioned” more than a day earlier.

US Navy Capt Tim Hawkins, a United States Central Command spokesperson, said in a statement the drone was surveilling regional waters when it malfunctioned “more than a day ago”.

Hawkins said the submersible was “defective” and an older model “that neither collected sensitive data nor carried any classified sonar or radar equipment”.

Operations in area waters continue, he said.

Earlier on Tuesday, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed that its naval forces “captured one of the most modern, unmanned, and smart submarines of the US terrorist army at the entrance to the strait of Hormuz”, according to Iranian TV.

The statement described the capture as a “complex intelligence and operational action at dawn” and said: “This submarine has now been captured and images of it will be released in the coming hours.”

Iran has maintained a blockade of the strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about one fifth of the global oil and gas shipments, since the outbreak of the war more than six months ago, while the US has imposed its own blockade of Iranian ports.

After a month of relative calm in August, Iran and the US have resumed exchanges of fire, sending ‌global oil prices back up to levels last seen in July.

Trump has struggled to end the unpopular war, which has claimed the lives of 18 US service members.

Iranian authorities have previously put the overall death toll from US and Israeli strikes in the thousands, figures that outside observers, including US-based monitoring groups, have broadly corroborated.

double quotation markThe ABC were told information they chose not to publish appropriately … because it is on a flood area by the Cooks River, when it rains and there’s flooding, raw sewerage goes into the Cooks River. That’s what it’s for – for fixing that.

I make no apologies for my electorate being serviced by me as a good local member, these three grants, they’re all appropriate.

Albanese also confirms he was made an honorary member of the club some 15 years ago, but doesn’t say whether he should have declared it.

double quotation markI don’t have a card. I don’t go in there. I haven’t been in there for years. I used to walk my dog along the path.

Criticism of One Nation candidate over illegal drug is ‘demeaning’ , says Joyce

Barnaby Joyce has again defended the Victorian One Nation leader, Warren Pickering, after Pickering yesterday in a press conference admitted to using ecstasy, methamphetamines and marijuana, losing his licence multiple times for drink driving and hurting people he loved.

Joyce says despite the admission, he has no qualms about One Nation’s vetting process, because Pickering had already spent time in the Australian Defence Force.

Speaking to News24, Joyce can’t say whether One Nation knew about the issues.

double quotation markI think it’s a little bit demeaning for even us to sort of have some sort of salacious analysis of what was happening to an individual two decades ago. Look, as any organisation grows, the speed One Nation’s growing and the membership grows, of course, you know, the requirements grow as well, but I’m satisfied in how we are going, we’re getting a lot more proficient at it.

And if people are saying, well, I’m not satisfied with Mr Pickering, you’d say, well, hang on, the Australian Defence Force was. They took him on board, and they most definitely have a vetting process, because I’ve been there myself.

I don’t know [if One Nation knew], you’d have to ask the people beforehand. For me, he was subsequently in the Australian Defence Force, they have a vetting process.

Anthony Albanese wins charity tennis match against a critic – 6-0 6-0 6-0

You might remember earlier this year, Joseph Daoud, a Sydney mortgage broker, won a charity auction at the midwinter ball to play a tennis match at the prime minister’s lodge with Anthony Albanese himself.

Well yesterday that game finally happened – and it was doughnuts for Daoud.

Daoud has spent big bucks putting up billboards and posters around the country critical of Labor’s changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax, and while in the capital yesterday, paid for some skywriting that spelled out “stop the tax”.

Albanese tells ABC News Breakfast “it was what it was”.

double quotation markBut for me, the main point is that it was raising funds for charity. I think it would have been good if the gentleman had have put some of the money he’s put into billboards and sky writing and all of that, given additional money to St Vincent’s, to Red Kite, a charity that provide support for the families of children who have cancer and for a good cause.

Daoud on Sunrise accused the PM of manufacturing the score and taking a 15 minute “tinkle” during the match. Asked about that on the Seven program, Albanese shrugged it off.

double quotation markWe played a match. It was for charity. Importantly, the score was six love, six love, six love. Was played in played in good spirits.

Albanese admitted that he had used the word “tinkle” but that it was “about two minutes”. I hated writing that.

Anthony Albanese has defended a grant handed to a golf club in his electorate, and said he makes “no apology” for it.

The grant was part of an infrastructure program that disbursed most of its money to safe, marginal or target Labor seats.

Over on ABC News Breakfast, Albanese says there were three grants in that program handed to his seat, and the funding for the golf club was to stop sewage from the course going into the local river during rain events.

double quotation markThe ABC were told information they chose not to publish appropriately … because it is on a flood area by the Cooks River, when it rains and there’s flooding, raw sewerage goes into the Cooks River. That’s what it’s for – for fixing that.

I make no apologies for my electorate being serviced by me as a good local member, these three grants, they’re all appropriate.

Albanese also confirms he was made an honorary member of the club some 15 years ago, but doesn’t say whether he should have declared it.

double quotation markI don’t have a card. I don’t go in there. I haven’t been in there for years. I used to walk my dog along the path.

Labor ‘not waving the white flag’ on illicit tobacco, but Albanese won’t completely rule out excise cut

Anthony Albanese says the government’s priority is still to crack down on criminals, over reducing the tobacco excise to curb the exploding black market.

But asked several times whether he’ll guarantee that the government won’t cut the excise, Albanese won’t actually confirm.

double quotation markAlbanese: What we want to do is to make sure that we continue to put that downward pressure on smoking rates and making vapes available everywhere isn’t going to help.

Albanese: What we’re saying is the big thing that we have to do is to crack down on crime …

Host: Are you saying you guarantee there will be no cut to the tobacco excise under a Labor government?

Albanese: No, what I’m guaranteeing is we’ll take on the criminals. That’s what we’re doing … We’re not about to wave the white flag.

Albanese dismisses concerns over powers in digital duty of care bill

Anthony Albanese says the Nationals leader, Matt Canavan, is being “disingenuous” over his criticisms that the communications minister, Anika Wells, will have too much power under the new digital duty of care legislation.

Speaking to the Today Show, the prime minister says the changes will be disallowable, meaning the Senate would have the power to vote against and reject rule changes.

Yesterday Wells outlined six areas that platforms would have to protect children from and ensure adults aren’t shown illegal content.

double quotation markThe eSafety commissioner will of course provide the advice, but Matt Canavan actually knows that he’s being disingenuous because all of these things will be disallowable. That is, will be up to the whole parliament, like the other previous laws have been.

Migration makes up almost half of regional Australia’s population growth, a report has revealed, as healthcare services warn of major workforce shortages if the intake is cut, AAP reports.

Research from the Regional Australia Institute shows migrants made up 46.2% of growth in 2025, with the largest cohort arriving in areas outside capital cities aged between 25 and 44.

The institute is calling for increased regional migration pathways to be placed at the centre of the nation’s population planning to address skills shortages, and support new economic activity.

Regional Australia had just over 17% of overseas migrants in the 2024/25 financial year, well below its 36% share of the national population.

Under current policy settings, 28% of Australia’s population growth is projected to go to the regions, according to the institute.

But it argues its modelling shows that figure could reach as high as 72% under a “nation-building approach” that prioritises the regions as a primary destination for population growth.

Grants program for target seats an idea ‘as old as ancient Greece’, says Clare

Jason Clare has denied accusations of pork-barrelling against the government over an “invite-only” community infrastructure grants scheme that handed the majority of its money to safe, marginal or key Labor seats.

Clare says it’s “democracy” that election promises – like funding for a new park or sports oval – are kept by a government.

double quotation markThat’s democracy … if you’re in an election campaign and you make a promise as the local member, people expect that you’ll deliver on it. And that’s what this fund does.

Clare is asked point blank whether this is the way Labor wins elections, through these sweeteners for voters. He says this isn’t a new tactic.

double quotation markI don’t think that that is new. This is probably as old as ancient Greece. Good politicians know that you don’t necessarily win elections by having a chat on the telly. You do it by having a chat on the front door of people’s homes and meeting people where they are.

Kids need a ‘digital detox’ says education minister

The education minister, Jason Clare, says the results of a global study released overnight shows Australian students who are online more do worse in class, and need a digital detox.

The 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment (Pisa) results found year nines were going backwards in reading and maths, despite maintaining above-average OECD results, and that public school students are more than two years behind their independent counterparts.

Speaking to ABC News Breakfast, Clare says:

double quotation markThe experts call this cognitive stunting, that technology can be used as a crutch in the classroom. Or it also can be a distraction.

We’ve taken mobile phones, personal phones out of schools. But you go into the average classroom today and you’ll see tablets and laptops on every desk in every classroom … And the evidence is telling us that we probably need a good digital detox in our schools.

It doesn’t mean that there’s no place for technology. Our kids need to learn digital skills, and that includes AI. They need to know how to use it and how not to use it. But if it’s everywhere, then it’s having negative impacts on our kids.

Clare says the UK, which improved its scores since the last test three years ago, implemented phonics and other key changes to their curriculum 10 to 15 years ago which Australia is doing now. He says the next meeting of state and territory education minister will consider reforms to the maths curriculum.

Labor’s digital duty of care bill risks ‘malicious compliance’, Greens say

Greens senator Sarah Hanson-Young says the government’s digital duty of care legislation is too vague on whether it allows users to opt-in or opt-out of algorithms, and says that risks manipulation or malicious compliance by the platforms.

Speaking to RN Breakfast this morning, Hanson-Young says the fines of up to $100m also won’t be enough to deter big tech.

double quotation markIt’s neither opt-in nor opt-out. And what I’m concerned about is how the tech platforms will manipulate that. Unless the rules are tight, unless there’s no gaps, big tech is going to spend a lot of money fighting these laws in the first place and finding every which way to get around them. Malicious compliance at best.

I think the fines element is one of those areas that I think is just not good enough … you need to hit them really where it hurts, and that’s their revenue. So it should be a percentage of global revenue.

Asked about the Coalition’s claims that the laws amount to censorship of free speech, Hanson-Young says Angus Taylor is “wrong”.

double quotation markI don’t know whether this is deliberate misinformation by the opposition leader or he just doesn’t know what he’s talking about. He hasn’t really spent much time engaging on these issues. Either way, it’s wrong.

Good morning, Krishani Dhanji here with you as we tick over the halfway mark of the sitting week!

There’s plenty to get to this morning so let’s get stuck in.

The Reserve Bank’s deputy governor has acknowledged Australians are “furious” about inflation while warning it is the “one big problem” the country’s economy is facing.

The RBA board is due to meet at the end of the month, as fears grow that it will hit mortgage holders with a fourth rate hike this year after inflation eased in July but less than expected.

Speaking to the ABC’s 7.30 on Tuesday evening, Andrew Hauser, the RBA’s deputy governor, said while the economy was doing “quite well” on low unemployment and real household incomes, inflation remained “too high”:

double quotation markPeople want inflation down. People are furious about inflation and I understand why. It’s unfair... It hits people on low incomes. It damages price signals. It makes the job of companies difficult.

double quotation markWhat they want us to do is our job and bring inflation down.

Hauser pointed to the ongoing Middle East conflict, the “unexpected global boom” driven by AI and the weakness of supply potential in Australia’s economy as risk factors for driving inflation.

While Hauser said a rate hike was not inevitable, he said the RBA was focused on bringing inflation down.

Victorians could pay almost $100 a year more for electricity under a state Coalition policy to halt two key transmission projects, according to new analysis that suggests it would result in a near 40% increase in wholesale prices by 2031.

Analysis by consultancy Nexa Advisory, commissioned by non-profit group Environment Victoria, has found postponing the Western Renewables Link and the VNI West would delay other renewable energy projects. Such a move could force the state to rely on using more gas.

As a result, the average wholesale electricity price could rise from $52.9 to $85.20 per megawatt hour – an increase of 37% – between 2027 and 2031. This would flow through to households, adding $472 to the power bills of a typical household – and up to $4,719 for a small business and $11,797 for a large business - over the five-year period.

By 2050, delaying the projects could add $33bn to wholesale electricity costs and produce an additional 8.6m tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions – akin to about a quarter of the state’s current annual electricity emissions.

Jim Chalmers says the Coalition and One Nation would “diminish or destroy” a compulsory super regime that this month’s intergenerational report will confirm is key to long term budget sustainability in a rapidly ageing society.

In remarks to the Super Members Council later this morning, the treasurer will condemn as “crazy” the right wing parties’ plans to give workers early access to their super savings, which he said would leave Australians poorer in retirement and weigh on the nations’ finances.

New Treasury projections show the number of retirement-age Australians will nearly double to around 9 million by 2066.

But the intergenerational report, to be released on 21 September, will show the share of older people on the aged pension is expected to fall from 66% to 52% in 40 years’ time.

As a result, spending on age and service pensions is projected to fall from 2.3% of GDP last year, to 1.8% in 2066, the IGR will show.

This is much lower than other nations, which are struggling to meet their pension obligations: aged pension costs in the UK will account for nearly 10% of GDP by 2060, 8% in Canada, 7% in New Zealand, and 6% in the US.

“Super takes serious pressure off social security outlays, and makes the budget much more sustainable as a consequence,” Chalmers will say.

double quotation markWe cannot let One Nation, the Liberals and Nationals diminish or destroy one of the best things Australians and Australia have going for us now and in the decades to come.

They would put at risk the fiscal sustainability, higher living standards and stronger economy that the IGR shows will be supported by a strong and maturing super system.

Welcome to Guardian Australia’s live news coverage for Wednesday.

Our terrific liveblogger Krishani Dhanji will be with you shortly.

articles.body_text:
Who: Napoli vs Arsenal
What: UEFA Champions League
Where: Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples, Italy
When: Wednesday at 9pm local time (1900GMT).
How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 16:00 GMT ahead of our live text commentary stream.

Napoli and Arsenal are paired in titanic tussle to open their Champions League seasons as two league winners – in Serie A and the Premier League respectively – within the last two-season faceoffs.

The Gunners ended a 22-year wait to reclaim the English top flight last season, while also reaching the Champions League final where they were defeated by Paris Saint-Germain.

Napoli were dethroned as Italian champions by Inter Milan last season, but retain a squad capable of striking fear into any side in Europe.

Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at the mouth-watering matchup.

As the defending Serie A champion last season, Napoli was eliminated in the league phase after finishing 30th of the 36 teams in the Champions League.

Massimiliano Allegri replaced Antonio Conte as head coach after last season.

“We need to get 12 points to secure qualification,” Allegri said. “We know we’re up against a team that has just won the Premier League and reached the final of this competition. [Arsenal manager Mikel] Arteta has done well to get his defence organized and they concede very few goals.

“I had the fortune of [coaching] in two finals but I lost both of them,” Allegri said, referring to when he was at Juventus and the 2015 and 2017 finals, which were won by Barcelona and Real Madrid, respectively.

Napoli has lost two straight in Serie A, getting beat by Como and Inter Milan – going down 3-2 to the latter at the weekend.

Arsenal are on a four-game winning streak to start their latest campaign.

The Gunners beat Manchester City 3-0 in the Community Shield – the English season opener between the previous season’s league and cup winners – to start the run.

Coventry, Aston Villa and Chelsea have been downed in the league, in what has been a formidable start.

Nine goals have been scored so far, with only one conceded by the team not only regarded as the best defence in the world, but also the favourites lift the Champions League trophy.

The Opta supercomputer has given Arsenal a 52 percent chance of winning the game, while offering Napoli only a 22 percent chance.

This will be the fifth meeting between the teams with Arsenal winning three of the encounters and Napoli claiming victory in the other match.

Napoli has issues in midfield for its Champions League opener against Arsenal on Wednesday, with both Scott McTominay and Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa unavailable.

McTominay underwent a surgical procedure to treat an irregular heartbeat on Tuesday, while Anguissa has a physical issue.

“In midfield we will play three between (Kevin) De Bruyne, (Billy) Gilmour, (Stanislav) Lobotka and (Antonio) Vergara,” Napoli coach Allegri said Tuesday.

Meret; Di Lorenzo, Marin, Rrahmani, Spinazzola; De Bruyne, Lobotka, Gilmour; Politano, Hojlund, Santos

Cristhian Mosquera has not travelled for the match due to a muscular injury that kept him out of the Aston Villa game.

Jurrien Timber continues his return from a groin injury and could make the bench. William Saliba remains out with a back problem.

Bruno Guimaraes, who was an unused sub at the weekend, is closing on full fitness.

Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie; Zubimendi, Rice; Saka, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz

articles.title: Liverpool vs Atletico Madrid: Champions League – preview, teams, prediction
articles.excerpt:
Who: Liverpool vs Atletico Madrid
What: Champions League, league phase
Where: Anfield, Liverpool, United Kingdom
When: Wednesday, September 9, at 8pm (19:00 GMT)
How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will b...
articles.body_text:
Who: Liverpool vs Atletico Madrid
What: Champions League, league phase
Where: Anfield, Liverpool, United Kingdom
When: Wednesday, September 9, at 8pm (19:00 GMT)
How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 16:00 GMT ahead of our live text commentary stream

Liverpool and Atletico Madrid kick off their 2026-27 Champions League campaigns with a mouthwatering league-phase game at Anfield.

Andoni Iraola got his first win as Liverpool manager over the weekend and now turns his attention to his first Champions League game with the football club.

Meanwhile, Atletico Madrid’s unbeaten start came to an end on Saturday when they slumped to a 3-0 away defeat at Athletic Bilbao.

Alexander Isak struck twice in the opening 10 minutes as Liverpool delivered a first win for Iraola with a 2-0 victory at Ipswich on Friday.

Isak’s Premier League record 125-million-pound ($169m) move from Newcastle was matched this week by Manchester City’s signing of Enzo Fernandez, but 12 months on, the Swede is finally beginning to deliver on his price tag.

Ipswich never recovered from a disastrous start as Liverpool cruised to victory at Portman Road with their latest 100-million-pound ($135m) signing Bradley Barcola making his debut as a second-half substitute.

Victory maintains an unbeaten start for Iraola. A pair of 2-2 draws against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest did not lack in entertainment for the Basque coach’s opening two games in charge, but did little to ease doubts over Liverpool’s ability to challenge at the top end of the table this season.

“We needed it. Definitely needed this one. Also the way it has been, I think, with a clean sheet,” said Iraola.

Athletic Bilbao thumped Atletico Madrid 3-0 in La Liga on a miserable Saturday afternoon for Diego Simeone’s side.

Simeone’s Atletico fell to their first defeat of the season, putting up little fight in the second half after Athletic made the breakthrough with two quick strikes from Nico Williams and Robert Navarro, before Oihan Sancet added a third at Bilbao’s San Mames Stadium.

“[We had] two minutes of inattention and poor decision-making in situations we should have handled better,” said Simeone. “Bilbao capitalised on that lapse.”

Striker Julian Alvarez, who tried to leave the club to join Barcelona this summer, returned as a substitute after illness in an ineffective second-half appearance.

“We were good in the first half, but the game got away from us in those [couple of] minutes,” said Simeone.

“We lacked in the second half everything that we had in the first.”

The Opta supercomputer pegs Liverpool as the favourites, with a win probability of 53 percent. Atletico were given a 23.5 percent chance of winning.

The two clubs have faced each other on nine occasions; Liverpool won four of the games, Atletico won three, and two ended as draws.

Liverpool seemed to be sailing with early goals from Andy Robertson and a typically fine strike by Mohamed Salah in their game last September, but were pegged back by Marcos Llorente’s goals in first-half stoppage time and at the 81st minute.

However, Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk soared to score with a header in the second minute of stoppage time to seal a 3-2 win for the Reds.

Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni have all been ruled out with injuries, while Federico Chiesa and Wataru Endo were not included in Liverpool’s Champions League squad.

Joe Gomez faces a late fitness test as he is struggling with a muscle issue.

New signing Bradley Barcola may be set for his start out wide on the right, with Victor Munoz dropping to the bench.

Alisson (goalkeeper); Araujo, Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez; Szoboszlai, Gravenberch; Barcola, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak

Forward Alexander Sorloth is expected to miss out on the game due to a thigh injury, and Arnau Ortiz is suspended after receiving a red card while last in European action – for Slask Wroclaw back in August 2024.

Oblak (goalkeeper); Llorente, Pubill, Romero, Grimaldo; Koke, Hjulmand; Simeone, Baena, Lookman; David

articles.title: Baker Mayfield and Buccaneers go from being at odds at start of camp to a monster contract to start season
articles.excerpt:
Baker Mayfield turned down a 2-year, $100 million extension with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, saying he felt

Baker Mayfield wasn't doing a new contract with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers once training camp b...
articles.body_text:
Baker Mayfield turned down a 2-year, $100 million extension with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, saying he felt

Baker Mayfield wasn't doing a new contract with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers once training camp began – until he did.

He was headed to free agency after this season – until he wasn't.

Funny how money has a way of changing things from one month to the next in the NFL.

PATRICK MAHOMES LEAPS PAST DAK PRESCOTT AS NFL'S HIGHEST-PAID QB WITH RECORD CHIEFS EXTENSION WORTH $504.75M

Mayfield has agreed to a three-year contract extension with the Bucs worth $165 million, OutKick has confirmed. The Bucs confirmed Mayfield isn't going anywhere.

The $55 million the quarterback will get on an annual average basis ties Mayfield with Joe Burrow, Josh Allen, Jordan Love, Trevor Lawrence and Matthew Stafford as the league's third-highest paid QBs.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield speaks during a post game news conference following an NFL football game against the New York Jets Sunday, Sept. 21, 2025, in Tampa, Florida. (AP Photo/Chris O'Meara)

Whether you think Mayfield should be in the same salary stratosphere as Burrow, Allen and last year's MVP is not the point.

They moved much closer to Mayfield's negotiating position in the past week or so and that's the reason they've locked up the player who has thrown 95 TD passes in 51 starts for them.

A reminder: This wasn't initially headed in this direction.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (6) makes a pass against Detroit Lions during the second half at Ford Field in Detroit on Oct. 20, 2025. (Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images)

The Bucs and their starting quarterback were at odds when training camp opened in July. The team had offered Mayfield a contract extension and he didn't believe it rewarded him to the extent he believed himself worth.

That led Mayfield to talk about a self-imposed training camp deadline for getting a new deal as being seemingly written in cement. It also led him to openly discuss betting on himself and the possibility of hitting free agency after the season.

There were wide-ranging pundit narratives that Mayfield plays better angry and we were about to see that this season.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (6) reacts against the Detroit Lions during the first half at Ford Field on Oct. 20, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Lon Horwedel/Imagn Images)

Mayfield's ire faded when the Bucs ignored the deadline and came back for more negotiations.

It outright disappeared when they offered him a deal that will keep him with the team and in a region he and his family like.

At a salary he obviously saw as more inviting than standing on negotiating deadlines and threats of 2027 free agency.

FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

Armando Salguero is OutKick's Senior NFL Writer.

articles.title: MAC files appeal to FBS committee to overturn Western Michigan-Michigan game, declare Broncos as winners
articles.excerpt: "Let me explain this to you. If it were the other way. And I don't give a damn what anybody thinks about this, I don't give a damn what anybody that never coached thinks about it. Never. If it were th...
articles.body_text:
"Let me explain this to you. If it were the other way. And I don't give a damn what anybody thinks about this, I don't give a damn what anybody that never coached thinks about it. Never. If it were the other way, Western Michigan would never, ever have been given a second to throw a ball into the end zone."

For a few minutes, the most stunning result of the early part of the college football season seemed to be the Western Michigan Broncos upsetting the heavily favored Michigan Wolverines at Michigan Stadium.

The Big House. Bryce Underwood, one of the most heavily promoted recruits of the past decade. New head coach Kyle Whittingham, known for his stability, consistency and avoiding major upsets while with the Utah Utes. And the Broncos took a 12-7 lead with just 38 seconds remaining and the Wolverines out of timeouts.

Everyone knows what happened next. Underwood's first Hail Mary attempt flew out of the back of the endzone, with the game clock on the broadcast and scoreboard showing 0:00. Game over. But after a poorly-explained review determined that there should have been an additional second added, Underwood was given a second opportunity. JJ Buchanan came down with it, and Wolverines fans stormed the field.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSIBLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Michigan fans storm the field after Michigan beat Western Michigan on a Hail Mary touchdown pass with time expired at Michigan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images (Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images)

Nearly everyone outside Michigan was perplexed, or downright angry, about the outcome. The Big Ten's explanation didn't make anything better either, with the conference saying the clocks were strobe-synced prior to the game, but that another clock viewed during the replay process had determined there was a second left. Even though the synced cameras showed zero seconds remaining.

Initially, it seemed like that would be the end of it. Western Michigan staff said they communicated with the Big Ten, reviewed the footage and were satisfied that proper procedure had been followed. Tuesday afternoon, though, that all changed.

The Mid-American Conference released a statement, announcing they'd filed a formal appeal to the NCAA FBS Oversight Committee and the College Football Playoff requesting that those two bodies recognize the Broncos as the true winners of the game.

"After further study and investigation, it is now evident that replay protocol was not properly followed in determining whether time remained on the game clock at the conclusion of the Western Michigan vs. Michigan football game," the statement says. "The established replay protocol requires that the game clock displayed on the program feed be used in determining whether time remained. Instead, the Big Ten Conference replay crew relied upon the clock feed embedded within its replay system. As a result, one second was placed back on the game clock and an additional play was awarded."

CRAIG CARTON BLASTS MICHIGAN FANS FOR STORMING FIELD AFTER CONTROVERSIAL WIN: 'THEY’RE A BUNCH OF MORONS'

Broc Lowry #12 of the Western Michigan Broncos looks on with seconds to play against the Michigan Wolverines at Michigan Stadium on September 05, 2026, in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Michigan won the game on a 47-yard touchdown pass with no time on the clock. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) (Gregory Shamus/Getty Images)

Interestingly, they also stress that the appeal isn't contesting the correct amount of time on the clock, just that the rules were improperly applied.

"This was not a judgment regarding the proper amount of time to place on the clock," it continues. "It was an error in the application of the established replay protocol governing this specific end-of-game timing situation. Had the protocol been properly followed and the program-feed clock been used, no additional play would have been awarded, and Western Michigan would have won the game, 12–7."

MICHIGAN FANS CALLED OUT ON SOCIAL MEDIA FOR RUSHING FIELD AFTER WOLVERINES STEAL WIN OVER WESTERN MICHIGAN

The conference, as a result, want the NCAA FBS Oversight Committee and College Football to recognize the Western Michigan Broncos as the "actual winner."

"The MAC is requesting that those bodies recognize Western Michigan as the actual winner of the game for purposes of their respective rankings, evaluations and selection deliberations, and take such other corrective action as may be within their authority," the statement concludes.

JJ Buchanan #6 of the Michigan Wolverines caught a game-winning pass with no time left to lift Michigan past Western Michigan 13-12 at Michigan Stadium on Sept. 5, 2026, in Ann Arbor, Mich. (Getty Images)

So what does the NCAA rule book actually say about this procedure, and does the MAC have a point? The closest relevant rule seems to govern what video evidence can be evaluated as part of a review. And while it's not overwhelmingly clear what the proper procedure should be, there is an indication that the "televised production" should be used when evaluating video evidence.

OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

"All reviews shall be based upon video evidence provided by and coming directly from the televised production of the game or from other video means available to the replay official that is also available to the television producer," the rule says.

So what chance does the MAC have at getting the result overturned? Very little. Even if there is some truth to this appeal, and the result was unfair to Western Michigan, it's a near impossibility that an FBS Committee overturns a result that was determined on the field. And it goes without saying that big programs like Michigan are a near-certainty to get the benefit of the doubt in these types of cases.

But the MAC at least showed some backbone and support for its member school after that debacle and what it cost them. Western Michigan may have contended for a College Football Playoff spot, with the benefit of a win over a top-20 opponent, had the game ended at 0:00.

In response, the Big Ten issued a statement of their own, saying, "The Big Ten stands by the statement released following the conclusion of the Western Michigan at Michigan game and the determination by the replay officials. We will have no further comment on the matter."

Sums up where both sides are, and why this controversy will never reach a satisfactory resolution for all involved parties.

articles.title: US supreme court blocks Missouri’s new congressional map backed by Trump
articles.excerpt:
Decision marks setback for president and Republicans, who set in motion  national redistricting battle last year

The US supreme court turned back an emergency appeal by Missouri officials to use a ne...
articles.body_text:
Decision marks setback for president and Republicans, who set in motion  national redistricting battle last year

The US supreme court turned back an emergency appeal by Missouri officials to use a newly drawn congressional map backed by Donald Trump in the November midterm election, letting stand a ruling by the state’s highest state court that blocked the new lines from taking effect.

Last week the Missouri supreme court ruled that the map must go before voters to approve or reject the new districts, meaning it cannot be used in the November election. The president and Republicans fumed over the decision, with the president calling it “horrible, ridiculous, and unConstitutional”.

Catherine Hanaway, the state’s Republican attorney general, had immediately pledged to appeal to the supreme court. The conservative Justice Brett Kavanaugh denied the emergency request.

The decision marks a rare setback for Trump and Republicans, who set in motion a national redistricting battle last year.

articles.title: American Bishop Robert Barron calls out St. Paul's Cathedral in UK over nightclub partnership
articles.excerpt:
Bishop Robert Barron condemns the "demonization" of the Trump administration by Catholics on the left.

Bishop Robert Barron criticized London’s historic St. Paul’s Cathedral on Monday over its new pa...
articles.body_text:
Bishop Robert Barron condemns the "demonization" of the Trump administration by Catholics on the left.

Bishop Robert Barron criticized London’s historic St. Paul’s Cathedral on Monday over its new partnership with a nightclub company, arguing the venue's upcoming concert series undermines its status as a sacred space.

The Christian Post reported that the Church of England is facing widespread backlash after St. Paul’s Cathedral in London signed a multiyear agreement to host concerts inside the building with Fabric, a nightclub company that lost its license approximately 10 years ago after two drug-related deaths. While the cathedral has worked with the nightclub company before, this latest agreement has sparked an international firestorm of controversy.

Though St. Paul’s belongs to the Anglican Church rather than the Roman Catholic Church, Barron — a prominent American Catholic bishop — wrote a lengthy social media post arguing against misusing the cathedral.

"Word has just come down that St. Paul’s Cathedral in London — the second most important church in the Anglican world — has imitated Canterbury Cathedral in permitting ‘raves,’ nightclub-like entertainments, to take place in its confines," he began.

TOURIST'S CHURCH CLOTHING HACK LEAVES TRAVELERS SHARPLY DIVIDED OVER SACRED-SITE ETIQUETTE

St Paul's Cathedral in London, England, is one of the British Isles' most famous sacred places, and has been widely criticized for its new agreement. (Dan Kitwood/Getty Images)

He blasted those who have already emerged to defend the move, saying "The usual reasons for acquiescing to this have been trotted out: reaching out to the young, trying to get with the times, etc. But this development simply shows that the leadership of the Church of England has lost any sense of the crucial distinction between the sacred and the secular."

Barron argued that the whole point of a sacred space is that it is specifically set apart from the mundane, secular world and is meant to "reorient us toward the divine."

"Accordingly, in the properly sacred space, one is lifted out of the conventional and introduced into the numinous. This is why Christian cathedrals are filled with images of the saints and angels and why their interiors are meant first to disorient us and then to reorient us toward the divine," he wrote.

"The contemporary West is, quite literally, the first culture in human history that is in danger of collapsing the sacred into the secular, or better, losing any sense of the difference between the two," he added further. "This is doing enormous damage, especially to young people, whose lives have been flattened into a preoccupation with money, worldly success, and material things. The Church indeed should go out into the secular space to find those who have wandered away from God, but it should then lead those wanderers back to the holy."

EXCLUSIVE VIDEO: BISHOP BARRON TO ADDRESS 'TRUE THREAT TO DEMOCRACY' AT TRUMP PRAYER EVENT

Bishop Robert Barron warned that part of the reason churches are filled with sacred iconography is specifically because they are a break from the mundane and secular, and thus, filling them with secular entertainment undermines that purpose. (Getty Images)

He concluded, "Having ‘raves’ in the nave of one of the most sacred spaces in the Christian world is, I’m sad to say, another sign of our pitiful surrender to ideological secularism."

According to the BBC, the events held at the event venue will be concerts rather than raves.

"Under the partnership, Fabric will be the cathedral's exclusive partner for such events until 2030. The first concert is due to take place on 29 October, although the artist has not been announced," the BBC reported. "Fabric co-founder Cameron Leslie called the deal ‘an extraordinary and unexpected coming together of two very different parts of London.’"

The BBC quoted Sandra Lynes Timbrell, the cathedral's director of visitor engagement, who expressed hope that a "carefully curated programme of exceptional concerts" would draw people who otherwise had not visited the cathedral.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Bishop Robert Barron is one of the most prominent Catholics in American public life. (Photo by Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

The controversy mirrors a 2024 dispute at Canterbury Cathedral, which hosted sold-out 90s "silent discos" that critics mocked as a "rave in the nave."

More recently, Canterbury cathedral featured the "Hear Us" art installation, using large stickers simulating graffiti, reportedly inspired by working with "marginalised communities and a team of skilled artists to create vibrant handwritten literature responding to the question: ‘What would you ask God?’" The project was conceived by poet Alex Vellis and curator Jacquiline Creswell.

Fox News Digital reached out to Bishop Robert Barron and Saint Paul's Cathedral and did not receive an immediate reply.

While cathedral leaders argue secular events help attract younger generations, some young believers say church leaders are misjudging what youth actually want.

Catholic actor David Henrie recently told Fox News Digital that he sees young people turning away from secular trends and seeking out traditional faith. Henrie noted an uptick in youth attending traditional Latin Mass services in the United States specifically because they are searching for a clear contrast to modern culture.

"I've seen it coming. I was one of those people who was not living a Christian life and then suddenly found the world was completely empty and was searching for something other worldly," Henrie said. "That's why I think you're seeing kids flock to the faith right now. It's because they're tired of the world."

"[T]hey want 'Lord of the Rings Catholicism,'" Henrie said. "You know, they want bells, smells, ancient expressions of the liturgy. That's where the young people are flocking right now. That's why you're seeing the Latin Mass booming."

Catholic leaders across the U.S. have reported sharp increases in the number of adult converts. A recent Gallup poll also found that 42% of young men now say religion is "very important" in their lives, a 14-percentage-point jump from the previous year.

Fox News' Kristine Parks contributed to this report.

Alexander Hall is an associate editor for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to Alexander.hall@fox.com.

articles.title: Legendary sports agent warns MLB lockout would be 'remarkably self-destructive' with CBA set to expire
articles.excerpt:
Leigh Steinberg tells OutKick in a recent interview why a lockout would be crippling to Major League Baseball amidst its resurgence.

Major League Baseball is just a few weeks away from the postseason...
articles.body_text:
Leigh Steinberg tells OutKick in a recent interview why a lockout would be crippling to Major League Baseball amidst its resurgence.

Major League Baseball is just a few weeks away from the postseason as the regular season winds down, but the sport has a different feel this year than in previous years.

Why? The threat of a lockout. The collective bargaining agreement between MLB and the MLBPA expires in December, and the owners are all but guaranteed to lock the players out. Legendary sports agent Leigh Steinberg said this is the "murkiest" environment the sport has had since before the turn of the century.

"This is the murkiest environment that baseball's had since they had the strike back in 1994. Owners seem determined to put in place a salary cap," Steinberg told OutKick in a recent interview.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred speaks during the Baseball Hall of Fame awards presentation in Cooperstown, N.Y., Saturday, July 26, 2025. (AP Photo/Seth Wenig)

Steinberg pointed to two major signings by the two-time defending World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers as the straws that broke the camel’s back and outraged owners to the point of wanting a salary cap.

"If you think about it, the contract that signaled all the outrage and incentivized owners to fight for a salary cap was the signing of Kyle Tucker and the thought that who's not playing that well this year, but it was the signing of Kyle Tucker and Edwin Díaz said to people, well, they're doing what the Rams just did," Steinberg said.

As Steinberg said, Tucker has struggled mightily in his first season after signing a four-year, $260 million contract. In 136 games this season, Tucker is hitting just .221 with 12 home runs and 59 RBI with an OPS of just .672.

Those numbers are well below the four-time All-Star’s career batting average of .265 and career OPS of .836.

The Dodgers signed Díaz to a three-year, $69 million contract to become the team’s closer, but the former New York Mets star has been hampered by injuries and has disappointed when on the mound.

LEGENDARY SPORTS AGENT TALKS ABOUT THE RAMS USE OF 'CAPONOMICS' TO BRING AARON DONALD OUT OF RETIREMENT

A locked padlock and chain against two official MLB baseballs representing a potential lockout between MLB and the Major League Baseball Players Association (MLBPA) for the 2027 season. (David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Díaz, who has been limited to just 16 games because of elbow and neck injuries, has a startling 11.85 ERA in 13 2/3 innings pitched with seven saves. Like Tucker, those numbers are out of the ordinary for him, as he has a career ERA of 3.06 across his 10 seasons in the major leagues.

Yet despite those signings not panning out, the owners are hell-bent on a salary cap, while the players are vehemently opposed. Steinberg warns of dire consequences if the two sides can’t come to an agreement soon.

"[A lockout] would be so self-destructive for baseball. The last time they did that was in 1994. The next year, the gross receipts went down 40%. Fans were angry. They didn't want to come to the games. And it took the steroid-fueled home run race between Mark McGwire and Sammy Sosa and then later Barry Bonds to bring the sport back," Steinberg said.

"It would be remarkably self-destructive."

Steinberg pointed out that revenue has been strong for owners as baseball has seen a resurgence.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Leigh Steinberg speaks onstage during the 39th Annual Leigh Steinberg Super Bowl Party at Storek on Feb. 7, 2026 in San Francisco, Calif. (Jesse Grant/Getty Images)

"What happens is you need to be able to put yourself in the heart and mind of the other side to negotiate a contract. So, are owners claiming economic turmoil and difficulty?" Steinberg said.

"And the answer is no, because the TV money and attendance and merchandising and fantasy and gambling now. The revenue streams are huge and baseball's had a resurgence."

The famed agent warned of the dire consequences the sport could suffer if both sides lose sight of what is at stake.

"When you get powerful billionaires owning teams locked in with wealthy players, you know, millionaires against billionaires, if you don't have someone able to see the larger picture, you can get deadlocked," Steinberg said.

Both sides have made proposals, but it doesn’t appear that any serious progress has been made in the preliminary talks. In March 2022, the two sides ended a 99-day lockout when MLB and the MLBPA ratified the new collective bargaining agreement.

Leigh Steinberg attends the 39th Annual Leigh Steinberg Super Bowl Party at Storek on Feb. 7, 2026 in San Francisco, Calif. (Jesse Grant/Getty Images)

With owners seemingly more dug in on a salary cap now than they were in 2022, there is concern that both sides would be willing to sacrifice games to get what they want.

Which, as Steinberg said, would be "incredibly self-destructive."

Steinberg, who was inducted into the California Sports Hall of Fame in 2017, has had many high-profile clients throughout his impressive career. Across football and baseball, Steinberg’s clients include Steve Bartkowski, Steve Young, Troy Aikman, Warren Moon, Bruce Smith, Thurman Thomas, Kordell Stewart, Jeff George, Ben Roethlisberger, Myron Rolle, Matt Leinart, Mark Brunell, Ricky Williams, Howie Long, Eric Karros and Dusty Baker, among others.
